title: Isopiestic Determination of the Osmotic Coefficients of Aqueous Na2SO4, MgSO4, and Na2SO4-MgSO4 at 25 C
authors: Joseph A. Rard and Donald G. Miller
journal: J. Chem. Eng. Data 26 (1), 33-38 (PDF first page, p. 33, is the end of an unrelated article on group surface areas and solubility; this paper begins lower on p. 33)
experimental_method: Isopiestic method at 25.00 C with KCl and H2SO4 reference standards; molalities are the average of two samples; saturated-solution molalities also determined by equilibration.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature 25.00 +/- 0.005 C (IPTS-68); isopiestic molalities known to at least +/-0.1 % (usually +/-0.05 % or better); KCl solubility 4.8088 +/- 0.0020, Na2SO4.10H2O 1.9526 +/- 0.0013, MgSO4.7H2O 3.0211 +/- 0.0022 mol/kg.
quality_remarks: Text layer clean; Table I read via word coordinates and compared against the page image. Four MgCl2 points are low concentration with up to 8 week equilibration. Rows at supersaturated concentrations are flagged by the authors only by text. Reference-standard osmotic coefficients are computed from literature equations, not measured.
not_extracted_tables: Table III: freezing-point-depression and vapor-pressure data for Na2SO4 (literature data recalculated by the authors, derived)
Table IV: freezing-point-depression data for MgSO4 (literature, recalculated)
Table VI: smoothed osmotic and activity coefficients (smoothed, derived)
extraction_notes: Table I columns assigned by x-coordinate of the words; row-by-row blank pattern checked against the image (all 62 rows). Footnote letters were glued to three numbers (4.8088a, 3.0211b, 1.9526c) and moved to the note column. Sanity: KCl molality and Phi KCl fall monotonically down the table until the minimum near 0.8968; Phi minimum is expected for KCl. Whole-page image read matched all cells I checked; Table II digits read from image.
